dialog.body: City of Newport Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?
Hi, yes. Um, my name is Dulce Pina. I'm calling about a parking ticket, but it's not mine, it's, well, it's sort of my mother's. Or it was a rental car. [pause] It's complicated.
All right, Ms. Pina. Let's take it one piece at a time. Is the ticket in your mother's name, or in yours?

That's the thing, I don't know. It came in the mail from the rental company. Not from the city. A letter from the rental company saying they got a ticket from Newport and they paid it and now they're charging her. Plus fees. There's a whole list of fees.

I see. When a vehicle is rented, the citation is issued to the registered owner of the vehicle, which would be the rental company. Companies often pass it along to the renter and add their own administrative charges.
Okay, but as I said before, she didn't even park there. Well, I mean, she did park there, but she was only there a few minutes. She's seventy-six. She went to pick up a prescription.
Ms. Pina, you said as you said before. Have you called this office previously about this?
No, no, that's just, it's how I talk. Sorry. This is the first time I'm calling. [sighs] I just keep saying it.
That's quite all right. Do you have the citation number in front of you? It should be on the letter, or on a copy of the ticket they enclosed.
Hold on. Let me find my glasses. [pause] Okay. There's a bunch of numbers. There's one that says reference, and one that says invoice, and one that says citation. Which one do you want?
The citation number, please. It's usually the one labeled citation or ticket number.
Okay, it says, hang on, it's four, seven, two, nine, one, and then a dash, zero three.
Four, seven, two, nine, one, dash, zero three. Let me pull that up. One moment, please.
Sure. Take your time.

Thank you for waiting. I do have that citation. It was issued for an expired meter on a Thursday afternoon in late November. The original fine has been paid by the rental company, which is what you described.
So the city got paid already? Then why does the letter say she owes more? It says one amount for the ticket and then another amount that's, like, double.
The city's portion would be only the fine on the citation. Any additional charges would be the rental company's own fees. Those are between them and the renter, and this office doesn't set them.
Hmm. So I can't dispute the fees with you.
Correct. You would take that up with the rental company. What you can dispute with the city is the citation itself, if you believe it was issued in error.
Okay, okay. But wait, if they already paid it, can she still, what is it, contest it?
There may still be a way to request a hearing. Let me look at what the record shows.
Because my friend, she said I have to be firm with you people. She said don't take no for an answer. So I'm being firm. [pause] Am I being firm?
You're being perfectly courteous, Ms. Pina.
Yeah, that's the problem. I'm not good at it. I'm really not. I get on the phone and I say okay, okay, and then I hang up and I think of everything I should've said.
Well, you have me on the line now, so let's cover everything. What would you like to ask?
Is there a hearing date? For this. Is there a date I should write down?
I'm not showing a hearing scheduled, because none has been requested on this citation. A hearing is generally set once a request is submitted in writing.
In writing. To who? To you? To the rental company?

To the city, not the rental company. The request goes to the Finance Department, referencing the citation number. The vehicle owner, in this case the rental company, is the party of record, so your mother would need to submit a statement and a copy of the rental agreement showing she was the driver.
Wait, so the rental company is the owner, but she's the one who has to ask? I don't understand. I thought if I called and said it's wrong, that's it.

I understand the confusion. Let me say it again. The ticket is on the car, and the car belongs to the rental company. The company paid it and billed your mother. If she wishes to contest the citation, she would send a written request that identifies the citation and explains her reasons, along with the rental paperwork.
Okay. So, written request, citation number, rental paperwork. And then they give her a hearing date.
Yes. A notice with the date would be mailed after the request is received and reviewed.
Mailed to where? Her house or the rental company?
To whatever address is provided in the request. I would suggest including her mailing address and a telephone number.
Can I use mine? Because she's not great with mail. She sets things down and then, you know.
You may list yours as a contact, but I would recommend she sign the request herself, since she is the one involved.
Okay. That's fair. [sighs] And is there some deadline? Because the letter is from, like, three weeks ago.

I don't see a deadline noted on the screen in front of me. I would not wait, though. If you like, I can transfer you to the parking violations clerk, who can confirm the time limit for requesting a hearing.
Yes, please. Yes. I'd rather know that than guess.
Let me check whether she's at her desk. Please hold.
Okay. Thank you. I'll hold.

Ms. Pina, I'm sorry, that line is not answering, and the office is going to be closed for the lunch hour. It's just about noon. They'll be back at one o'clock. Would you prefer to call back, or shall I leave a message?
Oh. Um. A message, I guess. Can you do that?
Certainly. May I have a callback number?
It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-two.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-two. And the message is that you are calling on behalf of your mother regarding citation four-seven-two-nine-one dash zero-three, to confirm the time limit to request a hearing.
Yes. And the hearing date, whether there's one. Say that I need to know what to send.
I'll add that. Anything else?
No, I think that's it. Wait, one more. The fees, the extra ones. I really can't do anything about those with you.
No, ma'am. Those would be handled with the rental company directly.
Okay. Okay. I'll call them. I'll try to be firm. Thank you, Ms. Whitcomb.
You're welcome. Have a good afternoon.
